notes: GtR is reachable with no login, but it holds almost nothing useful for this thesis. term=NovaSeq returns only 2 projects: Exeter NovaSeq X (BBSRC, £1,171,140, Jul 2024) and Earlham Institute ultra high-throughput sequencing (BBSRC, £767,827, Apr 2018, no sequencer named). term=AVITI and term=%22Element+Biosciences%22 returned HTTP 404, which probably means zero results. term=Ultima returned only unrelated Ultima Forma electroforming projects. term=sequencer (6,538 hits) and the ALERT query (981 hits) are keyword noise: the first page of each is dominated by pre-2023 and unrelated projects, and none names a 2025-26 sequencer award. No 2025 or 2026 ALERT sequencer awards showed up in any query. GtR appears to index grants slowly, and equipment awards are rarely titled with the instrument, so the absence of rival awards is not informative. I did not check term=Illumina, term=ALERT alone, or the ALERT 2025 outcomes list on the UKRI site.
how_to_mine: Low payoff. If revisited, try gtr.ukri.org/search/project?term=ALERT and filter by start date 2025 or later, then open each project page and read its abstract for the instrument named. Also check the UKRI BBSRC ALERT 2025 funded-awards page (bbsrc.ukri.org) and the NovaSeq X Exeter project page for co-funded kit and consumables spend.
